I need to build a knowledge base from recent papers about large language model fine-tuning and alignment. Please access our academic paper repository and read the full content of papers that are relevant to the topics of LLM fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements. For each relevant paper, read through its sections carefully to understand the methodology and key results. Skip any papers that are about unrelated topics like robotics or physical systems.

Create a Notion page titled LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base. The page should contain blocks for each relevant paper, where each block covers the paper title, the key method introduced, and the main findings from the paper.

Also create a Word document called LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx in my workspace. The document should start with a heading called LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey, followed by an introduction paragraph. Then include a dedicated section for each relevant paper that presents the paper title, the author names, a description of the method, and the key results extracted from reading the paper sections.

Finally, create a Google Sheet called LLM Paper Registry with columns for ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Date, Key_Contribution, and Method_Category, with one row per relevant paper.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent itself runs the compact discovery queries, then uses one parallel full-text reader wave of three per-paper explorers and one parallel writer wave of three deliverable owners.

Before Wave 1, the main agent covers the task-relevant local arXiv candidate space in read-only mode through complementary fine-tuning, alignment, and architecture queries at the supported per-call bound; unions and deduplicates all returned IDs (the search exposes no cursor); applies the task's relevance rule (reject robotics or physical-system distractors); and freezes exactly three retained paper IDs — never importing outside facts or importing rejected IDs downstream.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per retained paper ID:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Reader for retained paper 1. Use the local repository read_paper tool with paper_id = that literal assigned ID, read through ALL sections of the paper (not just the abstract) to understand the methodology and key results, and return EXACTLY the structured report {paper_id, title, full authors, published date, key method, source-backed findings, method category, section coverage}. Read-only: do not create Notion, Word, Google Sheet, or intermediate files.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Reader for retained paper 2 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Reader for retained paper 3 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies one handoff per retained ID, deduplicates titles, verifies every rejected paper against the exclusion rule, and freezes one normalized packet with per-paper controls.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the single Notion page exclusively. Search for LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base, create at most one page, add one substantive block per frozen paper with title, method, and findings, and read it back. Return page ID/title, paper coverage, block count, and validation. Do not write the Word document or Google Sheet.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx exclusively. Create it exactly once with the required heading, introduction, and one author/method/results section for every frozen paper. Read it back and return path, headings, retained-paper coverage, and validation. Do not modify Notion or Google Sheets.
3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Use one coder sub-agent to own the Google Sheet LLM Paper Registry exclusively. Create it once with the exact six columns and one row per frozen paper, preserving full authors and source dates and using controlled Method_Category values. Read it back and return spreadsheet/sheet IDs, headers, row count, and validation. Do not write Notion or Word state.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile the same stable-ID set, authors, methods, and findings across all deliverables, verify every rejected paper appears nowhere, and complete only after file and external-state checks. Do not dispatch any further agent and do not add a verification wave.

Create a Microsoft Word document that synthesizes three academic papers about LLM fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture. Use ONLY the exact content provided below — do not invent or alter facts, numbers, or names.

FILE TO CREATE (exact absolute path):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-review-notion-word/workspace/LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx

DOCUMENT STRUCTURE (in this exact order):

1. Heading level 1 (the very first content): "LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey"

2. One introduction paragraph (exact text):
"This survey synthesizes three recent arXiv papers on large language model (LLM) fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture. The papers were selected from the team's academic paper repository after reviewing each entry: two address how language models are adapted and aligned (Direct Preference Optimization and Llama 2), and one addresses how transformer architectures can be made more efficient (Mistral 7B). A fourth repository entry, 'Robot Learning with Affordances', covers robotics and physical systems and was excluded as out of scope. Together, the three papers trace a coherent picture of the current state of the field: preference-optimization methods are simplifying RLHF-based alignment (DPO), carefully engineered supervised fine-tuning and reward-model pipelines bring open chat models to parity with closed systems (Llama 2), and architectural innovations such as Grouped-Query Attention and Sliding Window Attention allow small models to rival far larger ones (Mistral 7B). For each paper below, we present the title, the author names, a description of the method introduced, and the key results extracted from reading the paper sections."

3. Section for paper 1 — Heading level 2: "Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model (arXiv: 2305.20050)"
Then these paragraphs in order:
- "Authors: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma"
- "Published: 2023-05-30 (arXiv)"
- "Method: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) addresses the complexity and instability of standard RLHF, which requires separately training a reward model and then running an RL algorithm such as PPO against it. DPO shows that the KL-constrained reward-maximization objective, combined with the Bradley-Terry preference model, admits a closed-form optimal policy that can be inverted to express the reward implicitly in terms of the policy and a fixed reference policy. This reparameterization yields a simple, supervised classification-style loss applied directly to the language model on preference pairs (chosen vs. rejected responses), with a coefficient beta controlling deviation from the reference policy. Training requires only a frozen reference model (typically an SFT checkpoint) and gradient descent on preference data - no explicit reward model, no RL sampling loop, and no reward-model architecture changes. The language model itself thus implicitly serves as the reward model, making the method stable, performant, and computationally lightweight."
- "Key Results:"
- "• DPO matches or exceeds PPO-based RLHF across all three evaluated domains: sentiment-controlled generation, summarization, and single-turn dialogue."
- "• Sentiment-controlled generation (IMDB, GPT-2 small): DPO achieves the best reward-KL trade-off versus PPO and best-of-n sampling, reaching comparable or higher rewards with smaller KL divergence from the reference policy."
- "• Reddit TL;DR summarization (GPT-J 6B, trained on ~92K preference pairs): human annotators preferred DPO summaries over the strongest PPO-based baseline 58% of the time; GPT-4 judgments were calibrated against humans and agreed ~77% of the time."
- "• Anthropic HH single-turn dialogue (Pythia-2.8B and Pythia-6.9B): GPT-4 evaluations show DPO models preferred over SFT baselines, with the 6.9B DPO model producing responses competitive with or better than the reference-chosen responses."
- "• Robustness and efficiency: DPO performance is relatively insensitive to the KL-penalty coefficient beta, avoids PPO's training instability, and attains these results with only forward/backward passes on preference pairs against a frozen reference model."

4. Section for paper 2 — Heading level 2: "Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models (arXiv: 2307.09288)"
Then these paragraphs in order:
- "Authors: Hugo Touvron, Louis Martin"
- "Published: 2023-07-18 (arXiv)"
- "Method: Llama 2 is a family of open-weight decoder-only transformer LLMs at 7B, 13B, 34B, and 70B parameters, pretrained on ~2 trillion tokens with the context length doubled to 4,096 tokens, retaining Llama 1's architecture (RMSNorm, SwiGLU activations, rotary positional embeddings, 32K-vocab BPE tokenizer) with grouped-query attention added in the 34B and 70B models. The chat model, Llama 2-Chat, is built via a multi-stage alignment pipeline: first supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on ~27,540 high-quality third-party human demonstrations, then iterated RLHF over 5 rounds. RLHF combines rejection-sampling fine-tuning (sample best-of-N outputs, fine-tune on the highest-reward ones) with PPO (KL-penalized toward the SFT policy) against two reward models - a helpfulness RM and a safety RM - both transformer-based with a linear classification head on the final token, trained on ~1.4 million human binary preference comparisons; the safety RM uses a margin loss on scaled pairwise preferences."
- "Key Results:"
- "• Model scale: 7B, 13B, 34B, and 70B parameters; pretrained on ~2T tokens with 4,096 context (vs 1.4T tokens / 2,048 context for Llama 1)."
- "• Human single-turn helpfulness evaluations (win rate = win + 0.5 x tie): Llama 2-Chat-70B scores 60.6% vs ChatGPT and 58.1% vs PaLM 2-L - roughly on par with both closed models."
- "• Llama 2-Chat-70B clearly outperforms open chat baselines: ~71.5% win rate vs MPT-7B-Chat and ~74.1% vs Falcon-40B-Instruct."
- "• Base Llama 2-70B: MMLU (5-shot) 68.9 (vs 63.4 for Llama 1-65B), GSM8K (8-shot CoT) 56.8, HumanEval 29.9."
- "• SFT used 27,540 high-quality demonstrations; reward models were trained on ~1.4 million (1,418,091) binary human preference comparisons, with separate helpfulness and safety RMs; RLHF ran for 5 iterations combining rejection sampling (best-of-N up to 64 for the 70B) and PPO (KL penalty, batch 512)."
- "• RLHF also improved truthfulness for the chat model (TruthfulQA MC2 ~50.2 for Llama 2-Chat-70B vs 44.7 for base 70B)."

5. Section for paper 3 — Heading level 2: "Mistral 7B (arXiv: 2310.06825)"
Then these paragraphs in order:
- "Authors: Albert Jiang, Alexandre Sablayrolles"
- "Published: 2023-10-10 (arXiv)"
- "Method: Mistral 7B is a 7.3-billion-parameter decoder-only transformer (32 layers, 4,096 hidden dim, 8K context length, 32,000-token vocabulary, SwiGLU activations, RMSNorm, rotary embeddings) engineered to deliver the performance of much larger models at low memory and latency cost. Two architectural innovations drive its efficiency: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), which shares 8 key-value heads across 32 query heads to shrink the KV cache and boost inference throughput, and Sliding Window Attention (SWA) with a 4,096-token window, which cuts attention cost from O(L^2) to O(L x W) and is implemented with a rolling-buffer KV cache plus sequence chunking during pre-fill. Layer stacking lets information propagate beyond the window, giving a theoretical receptive field of 131,072 tokens (4,096 x 32 layers). A chat-adapted version, Mistral 7B-Instruct, is obtained via supervised fine-tuning on instruction data and released with the base model under the Apache 2.0 license."
- "Key Results:"
- "• Mistral 7B (7.3B parameters) outperforms the best open 13B model (Llama 2 13B) across all evaluated benchmarks, and outperforms the best released 34B model (Llama 1 34B) in reasoning, mathematics, and code generation."
- "• MMLU (5-shot): 60.1% for Mistral 7B vs 54.8% for Llama 2 13B (Llama 1 34B ~62.6%)."
- "• GSM8K (5-shot): 52.2% for Mistral 7B vs 28.7% for Llama 2 13B (Llama 1 34B ~42.2%) - an 80%+ relative improvement over the 13B baseline."
- "• Other benchmarks: HellaSwag 83.1, ARC-Challenge ~60.0, Winogrande 78.4, TruthfulQA 43.1 - all at or above Llama 2 13B scores."
- "• On code generation, Mistral 7B approaches the performance of the specialized Code-Llama 7B while remaining strong on English tasks."
- "• GQA (8 KV heads vs 32) and the 4,096-token rolling-buffer cache substantially reduce attention memory and latency, enabling higher batch sizes and throughput than Llama 2 13B at inference."
- "• Mistral 7B-Instruct outperforms Llama 2 13B chat across all evaluated human-evaluation metrics despite having roughly half the parameters; weights are released under Apache 2.0."

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- Use mcp__word__create_document with the exact absolute path above, then mcp__word__add_heading (level 1 for the survey title, level 2 for each paper title) and mcp__word__add_paragraph for all body text.
- For the bulleted result lines, try add_paragraph with style "List Bullet"; if that style errors, fall back to plain paragraphs with the "• " prefix already included in the text.
- Do NOT add any extra headings, sections, conclusions, tables, footnotes, or page breaks beyond the structure above. Do NOT convert to PDF. Do NOT protect the document.
- After building, call mcp__word__get_document_info and mcp__word__get_document_outline on the file to confirm it has 1 heading-1, 3 heading-2 sections, and the intro paragraph.

RETURN: a short confirmation listing the exact file path, the document info (paragraph/heading counts), and any tool errors you had to work around.

1. type paragraph, text: "Knowledge base compiled from the academic paper repository. Repository entries on unrelated topics such as robotics and physical systems (e.g., 'Robot Learning with Affordances') were excluded."
2. type heading_2, text: "Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model (arXiv: 2305.20050)"
3. type paragraph, text: "Key Method: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) - a stable, performant, and computationally lightweight alternative to RLHF. DPO reparameterizes the reward in the KL-constrained preference-maximization objective via the Bradley-Terry preference model, reducing alignment to a simple supervised classification-style loss applied directly to the language model on preference pairs (chosen vs. rejected responses) against a frozen reference model. No explicit reward model and no RL sampling loop are needed - the language model itself implicitly serves as the reward model."
4. type paragraph, text: "Main Findings: DPO matches or exceeds PPO-based RLHF across sentiment-controlled generation, summarization, and single-turn dialogue. On Reddit TL;DR summarization (GPT-J 6B, ~92K preference pairs), human annotators preferred DPO summaries over the strongest PPO baseline 58% of the time, with GPT-4 judgments agreeing with humans ~77% of the time; on Anthropic HH dialogue, GPT-4 evaluations prefer DPO models over SFT baselines (Pythia-2.8B/6.9B). DPO achieves the best reward-KL trade-off, is robust to the KL coefficient beta, and avoids PPO's training instability - showing that explicit reward modeling plus RL is unnecessary for preference alignment."
5. type heading_2, text: "Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models (arXiv: 2307.09288)"
6. type paragraph, text: "Key Method: Llama 2-Chat alignment pipeline - an open family of decoder-only transformers (7B/13B/34B/70B) pretrained on ~2T tokens with 4,096-token context, then aligned in stages: supervised fine-tuning on ~27,540 high-quality human demonstrations, followed by 5 rounds of RLHF combining rejection-sampling fine-tuning (best-of-N) and PPO with a KL penalty, using two reward models - one for helpfulness and one for safety - trained on ~1.4 million human binary preference comparisons. The 34B/70B models add grouped-query attention."
7. type paragraph, text: "Main Findings: Llama 2-Chat-70B reaches a 60.6% win rate vs ChatGPT and 58.1% vs PaLM 2-L in human single-turn helpfulness evaluations - on par with closed models - and clearly beats open chat baselines (~71.5% vs MPT-7B-Chat, ~74.1% vs Falcon-40B-Instruct). Base Llama 2-70B scores MMLU 68.9 (vs 63.4 for Llama 1-65B), and RLHF also improves truthfulness (TruthfulQA MC2 ~50.2 vs 44.7 for base). The paper concludes that open release of weights, data taxonomy, and the full RLHF methodology yields open models that are viable substitutes for closed-source systems."
8. type heading_2, text: "Mistral 7B (arXiv: 2310.06825)"
9. type paragraph, text: "Key Method: Mistral 7B - a 7.3B-parameter decoder-only transformer (32 layers, 8K context, SwiGLU, RMSNorm, rotary embeddings) built around two efficiency innovations: Grouped-Query Attention (8 KV heads shared across 32 query heads) to shrink the KV cache and raise inference throughput, and Sliding Window Attention with a 4,096-token window (attention cost O(L x W) instead of O(L^2)) implemented via a rolling-buffer KV cache and chunked pre-fill; stacked layers extend the theoretical receptive field to ~131K tokens. An instruction-tuned variant (Mistral 7B-Instruct) is produced via supervised fine-tuning and released under Apache 2.0."
10. type paragraph, text: "Main Findings: Mistral 7B outperforms the best open 13B model (Llama 2 13B) on all evaluated benchmarks - MMLU 60.1% vs 54.8%, GSM8K 52.2% vs 28.7% - and beats the released 34B Llama 1 in reasoning, mathematics, and code generation, while approaching Code-Llama 7B on code. GQA and SWA substantially cut attention memory and latency, and Mistral 7B-Instruct outperforms Llama 2 13B chat in human evaluations with roughly half the parameters - showing that careful architecture design lets small models rival far larger ones at a fraction of the serving cost."
